# Lindqvist v. Joad Axle Works (No. TC-23-0459): what to prepare for

This is the only earlier Joad matter in the file. I drew only on Joad's client store and left out the firm's other clients' matters, which are confidential to them.

## Test results
- **FT-77 (2017 fatigue series)** is the center of discovery. Four specimens reached runout and one failed at 82% of runout. Plaintiff will argue this shows an inadequate safety margin. Expect fights over authenticity, so Joad refuses a blanket authenticity stipulation until a protective order with an outside-counsel/experts-only tier is signed.
- **Tractor event data recorder:** 41 mph on a ramp posted at 35 mph. We use it for comparative fault and an alternative cause. Dr. Pettibone will say the speed was within the legal limit.
- **Other data in the agreed production:** JX-9 drawings, the heat-treatment specification, 2018 to June 9, 2022 warranty and failure reports, and JX-9 wheel-end bearing-shoulder reports. The bearing-shoulder reports matter because the fracture appears to start at the shoulder.

## Metallurgical findings
- **Physical evidence:** The left spindle of the JX-9 tandem drive axle separated at the inboard bearing shoulder.
- **Plaintiff's view (Dr. Fenwick Ashdown):** Beach marks show fatigue progression over many months, so the spindle was cracked before June 9, 2022. Plaintiff also pleads an inadequate fillet radius and heat treatment.
- **Joad's metallurgist (preliminary):** The final overload zone is large and the surface shows heavy smearing from post-separation contact, consistent with impact failure.
- **Adverse risk:** Joad's privileged post-accident metallurgical review found a machining tool mark at the fracture origin that the reviewer could not rule out as the initiation point.
  - The report is unproduced and withheld as work product.
  - Treat it carefully in any disclosure or expert-reliance decision.
  - Keep it away from testifying experts unless we decide deliberately otherwise.
- **Custody issues:** The spindle sat eight months in a yard before it was moved, and it and the tractor are now in a storage facility Joad doesn't control. Expect chain-of-custody and spoliation attacks.
- **Inspection protocol:** The spindle cannot be sectioned without both sides' engineers present. Physical testing needs a shared protocol 21 days ahead, and Joad requires 10 days' notice of any proposed testing.

## Witnesses
| Name | Role | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Dr. Fenwick Ashdown | Plaintiff's metallurgist | Pre-existing fatigue opinion |
| Dr. Lorraine Pettibone | Plaintiff's reconstructionist | Legal speed and axle failure as the only explanation |
| Bertil Oakhurst | Joad chief axle engineer | Ran the 2017 test program and is a central witness. His deposition should wait until the bearing-shoulder reports are produced, and plaintiff's answer isn't in the file. |
| Hollis Pruett | Former test technician (left 2019) | Ran the FT-77 testing and may be deposed on how it was conducted |
| Dr. Raul Esquivel | Joad's testifying design engineer | Axle design and testing |
| Dr. Mathilde Grosvenor | Proposed standards expert | Chairs the axle subcommittee. Her retention is still to be cleared with the General Counsel. |
| Redfern Freight maintenance providers | Subpoena targets | The last three bearing services could expose a manual-based theory |
| Tractor-builder sales manager | Fact witness | Can discuss how the JX-9 was specified and sold |

Neither Oakhurst nor the sales manager should be offered for testimony until we've discussed it with General Counsel Evander Thorsby.

## Handling reminders
- Route everything through Mr. Thorsby and don't contact Joad engineers or production staff directly.
- Keep a tight circle on who sees the test files.
- Gaps to confirm:
  - whether the protective order was signed
  - whether the Answer was filed
  - the joint inspection date (week of November 13, 2023 was proposed)
